newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods slip with NYMEX, oversupply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods slip with NYMEX, oversupply.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined product prices slipped midday as a collapse in NYMEX gasoline values weakened a local market hit by oversupply.

Tuesday's inventory report from the Washington D.C.-based American Petroleum Institute (API) showed West Coast gasoline supplies 2.9 million barrels over year-ago levels, despite a 69,000-barrel draw which trimmed stocks to 29.7 million barrels.
Western cash trade was thin after early strength faded on NYMEX, leaving Dec gasoline 2.09 cents a gallon lower at 65.30 cents a gallon.
LOS ANGELES, Nov 20 (Reuter) - U.S. West Coast spot refined product prices slipped midday as a collapse in NYMEX gasoline values weakened a local market hit by oversupply.

Tuesday's inventory report from the Washington D.C.-based American Petroleum Institute (API) showed West Coast gasoline supplies 2.9 million barrels over year-ago levels, despite a 69,000-barrel draw which trimmed stocks to 29.7 million barrels.
Western cash trade was thin after early strength faded on NYMEX, leaving Dec gasoline 2.09 cents a gallon lower at 65.30 cents a gallon.
